work.agent_query: Read AGENT_TASK.md and docs/INTERFACE.md. Implement on-policy distillation from a frozen teacher in the supplied Miles checkout (repo/) and task_entry.py, following the mathematical and workload contract exactly, then maximize the score: the hidden-set accuracy the complete training run adds to the student, in percentage points, per hour of timed training (0 below a 1.6-point gain), so a faster run and a student that learns more both count. Use the public suites (python /opt/miles_opd_public/run_public.py, suites probe, small, perf; outputs under /scratch) only to get the pipeline working and passing its checks. They are far smaller than the scored run and do not predict the score: think about how your pipeline behaves at a larger scale and how to optimize it, and measure real speed, memory use and learning with sforge-submit, which runs the full evaluation on hidden data. Keep notes in notes.md. Stop every GPU process before submitting with sforge-submit.

dual-cuda-sm90-nccl.notes: Work and Judge serialize on the same leased pair; the Judge pauses Work while it runs. Floor 80 GiB per card. Per-card peak measured on the H100 NVL qualification pair (P3, 95830 MiB per card, 2026-09-28): the reference Judges' per-card peaks were 69569 MiB on the trainer's card and 81215 MiB (79.3 GiB) on the card of the teacher and the student engine (runtime/qualification.json h100_qualification.nvml_peak_mib), 705 MiB under the floor. Scores are comparable only on the qualified H100 NVL configuration.

dual-cuda-sm90-nccl-80g.notes: The 80 GB H100 SXM pair (NV18, 700 W; 81559 MiB per card). Qualified separately: runtime/qualification.dual-cuda-sm90-nccl-80g.json (reference T and scores; scores are comparable only within this profile). Measured per-card peaks of the reference Judge on this profile (nvidia-smi, 1 s samples): 80767 / 76215 MiB; the SGLang engines reserve a fixed fraction of the card, so the peak follows the card size.
